summary: Execution accounting records 5 experiments in 0.0 minutes, including 3 compute-bound tasks. All 5 entries tie at 0.0 minutes, so no compute-bound task is measurably slower and no phase-level cause can be assigned. The locked task attribution does not identify GPU idle on compute-bound work.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction has zero-minute resolution for all 5 entries, so the compute-bound leaders are tied and phase-level causes are not observable.
The point-in-time GPU snapshot is not linked to experiment execution windows, so compute-period utilization cannot be graded; the locked compute-task idle indicator remains false.
No task record declares concurrent model count or runner selection, so DualGPURunner eligibility and engagement cannot be audited.
improvements_suggested: Capture monotonic task start, task end, phase duration, and gate-wait receipts instead of relying only on disk modification times.
Link GPU samples to active task IDs and compute-bound declarations, and alert only when an active compute-bound task remains idle.
Persist loaded-model count and runner selection in each compute-task receipt; select DualGPURunner only when at least 2 models are loaded in parallel.
Add readiness-aware queue dispatch so work with satisfied prerequisites can proceed while unresolved gated work remains pending.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add readiness-aware dispatch with explicit prerequisite and gate-wait receipts.
Record task-scoped monotonic phase timing and task-correlated GPU samples.
Record loaded-model count and runner selection, with DualGPURunner chosen only for at least 2 parallel models.
meta_reflection: The reconstructed timing supports a duration tie, not a claim that execution was instantaneous. The idle GPU snapshot cannot be attributed to a running compute task, and no data available this milestone establishes parallel multi-model execution or DualGPURunner engagement.
